newsitem.title: PERU: Peru tax agency shames firms whose checks bounce.
newsitem.headline: Peru tax agency shames firms whose checks bounce.

text.p: Peru's tax collection agency resorted Friday to shaming companies paying their dues with checks that bounce by publishing offenders' names in the press.

The National Superintendency of Tax Administration (SUNAT) took out half-page advertisements in top newspapers announcing the names of 36 firms that were overdue on their contributions after their checks bounced during the fourth quarter last year.
"Seeing your company's name in the paper cannot be very pleasant," SUNAT spokesman Fernando Aguirre said in an interview. "It is an efficient way of letting the contributor know he is in debt."
SUNAT has an aggressive three-year tax collection programme agreed with the International Monetary Fund to raise revenues by 1998 to 25.5 percent of gross domestic product, from 24 percent in 1995.
